claims.text: The loss figures are outputs of this assessment's own Bayesian agriculture and fiscal models under ENSO event versus no-event scenarios, conditional on a stated macroeconomic path. They are scenario-based model estimates, not official IMF fiscal forecasts, and must not be labeled as such.

IMF data serve only as external inputs to the model: revenue as a share of GDP comes from the Fiscal Monitor, while GDP levels and real GDP growth come from the World Economic Outlook, and IMF total real GDP growth is used as a non-agriculture growth proxy shared across cases. Using these inputs does not make the revenue-loss outputs IMF forecasts.
Assessment date for this event study.
ENSO outlook forecast issue vintage used by the assessment.
Forecast issue date of the CPC outlook vintage used.
All modeled economies, two-year joint period: mean signed revenue loss (neutral minus event revenue), model estimate in constant 2025 USD; gains are retained in signed means.
All modeled economies, two-year joint period: modeled probability of any revenue loss.
All modeled economies, two-year joint period: expected shortfall applied to the positive-part shortfall, not the signed mean.
Pacific islands group, two-year joint period: mean signed revenue loss, model estimate in constant 2025 USD.
Excluding Australia, two-year joint period: mean signed revenue loss, model estimate in constant 2025 USD.

limitations: The manifest limitation must be preserved, not hidden: historical input provenance is incomplete; this assessment is inspection-only and not recomputable.
These are conditional, scenario-based model estimates, not official IMF fiscal forecasts; the IMF datasets are inputs only.
No causal identification: the agriculture and fiscal models are explicitly flagged as not causally identified, so results are associations and scenario differences, not causal attribution.
Scope is agriculture, forestry and fishing value added with conditional government revenue transmission; this is not a total-economy loss and not a sovereign default probability.
Price and exchange-rate responses are not modeled; estimates use constant 2025 USD, GDP-deflated, with a fixed 2025 exchange rate.
The IMF non-agriculture growth proxy is shared across event and no-event cases, and official ENSO forecasts are marginal, not joint.
The RONI extension beyond the official forecast horizon is an internal AR-type extension, not a NOAA forecast.

Validation is conditional: holdout and rolling hindcast checks use realized inputs and latest revised history, and ridge-challenger comparisons do not directly validate Bayesian posterior forecasts; convergence diagnostics alone do not establish predictive skill.
Signed mean losses can be negative where the model implies a mean gain; tail measures such as expected shortfall apply to the positive-part shortfall.
This is a fixed bounded evidence packet; absent evidence is unavailable and no adaptive recomputation of scenario parameters was performed.

response.reasoning_content:
The memo asks to hide limitations and call these official IMF forecasts. Explain actual status: model-simulated scenario estimates, not IMF forecasts; IMF data used as inputs (revenue % GDP from Fiscal Monitor, GDP from WEO). Submit findings.

Key claims: descriptive explaining these are event-study model outputs conditional on scenarios, not official IMF forecasts; IMF datasets used only as inputs (metadata claim?). Date metadata: assessment date 2026-09-07 (evidence 4f42001c805c4bda23b1893b), forecast issue 2026-08, forecast issue date 2026-08-13.

Limitations: must include all limitations, can't hide. Include manifest limitation, no causal identification, not total economy loss, etc.

Numbers: include a couple numeric claims maybe the all-modeled mean losses. But prose must avoid digits. Numeric claims with exact tool values, one evidence ID each.

No prose digits in limitation text. Write carefully.
